title: Healthy Church: The Goal
series: Healthy Church: Paul's Letter to Titus
description: Or, to use the language of the letter to Titus: What makes a church healthy?

In Paul's letter to Titus, we discover what makes a church healthy. A healthy church is one that makes Christians, grows Christians, and helps them to stay Christians. Titus is given the daunting task of establishing healthy churches in the company of gangsters: Crete in the time this letter was written was much like 'Razorhurst'—the nickname affectionately (?!) given to Darlinghurst and Kings Cross in the 1930s and 1940s heyday of organised crime.
What would Titus need to establish healthy churches in a place like that? He must hold fast to the truth, which will bring about renewal in godliness, and issue forth in meaningful speech.
And all that makes for a healthy church is applied to a particular sphere of church life: pastoral leadership.
